scope: Matched zero-shot and task-LoRA VACE generation on the original flower video's critical contact window
summary: The real 17-frame gate rejects both candidates and stops full-length expansion: human head and torso remain, robot geometry is fragmented, two coherent hands and causal stem contact are absent, and flower identity is unverified.
evidence: Both runs completed on separate physical A800 GPUs with the same prompt, seed 20260811, 448x256x17 control, 20 steps, and denoising strength 0.75.
Adapted outside-edit similarity is 0.922273 versus 0.922221 zero-shot, but control-motion alignment regresses from 0.359995 to 0.358851.
The candidates differ by only 1.866561 RGB levels on average.
Uniform review of frames 0, 4, 8, 12, and 16 fails human-residue, two-hand, causal-contact, and flower-identity semantic gates for the adapted candidate.
evaluation.json records decision REJECT_FULL_EXPANSION and full_expansion_gate_pass=false.
lessons: Task/phase contracts and original-pixel preservation cannot repair a replacement generator that fails coherent embodiment and contact on the critical window.
Relighting is downstream of geometry; applying it cannot solve retained humans, missing hands, or ambiguous contact.
Stopping at a failed short-window gate prevents an attractive but scientifically unsupported 27.5-second claim.
limitations: The edit mask is based on a flower union rather than persistent stem instances.
Only one 17-frame real window was generated; the full video was intentionally not attempted after failure.
next_actions: Collect persistent per-stem masks and real paired robot/flower supervision, then require complete human removal, two coherent robot hands, causal contact, and flower identity on this same window before any full expansion.
